title: Isomorphisms of sheaf modules are local on an open covering
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $X$, and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ let $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_X|_U$ and, for an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal M$, let $\mathcal M|_U$ be the $\mathcal O_U$-module $W\mapsto\mathcal M(W)$ ($W\subseteq U$ open) with the restriction maps and module structures of $\mathcal M$ [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]; for a morphism $\alpha:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules let $\alpha|_U:\mathcal M|_U\to\mathcal N|_U$ be the morphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules with components $(\alpha|_U)_W=\alpha_W$ for $W\subseteq U$ open. A morphism is an isomorphism if it has a two-sided inverse in the category of modules in question. Let $X=\bigcup_{a\in A}U_a$ be an open covering and $\alpha:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Then $\alpha$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules if and only if $\alpha|_{U_a}:\mathcal M|_{U_a}\to\mathcal N|_{U_a}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{U_a}$-modules for every $a\in A$.

proof.text: Restriction of module sheaves to Over (U i) is SheafOfModules.overFunctor, so it preserves isomorphisms. This proves the forward implication.

For the converse, apply the forgetful functor SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X) to the morphism. Mathlib proves that this functor reflects isomorphisms, so it suffices to show the underlying morphism of abelian sheaves is an isomorphism.
The hypothesis that the supremum of the opens U i is top gives a covering family for Opens.grothendieckTopology X by Mathlib Opens.coversTop_iff.

For each i, the restriction of the underlying abelian sheaf morphism via the topology overPullback is definitionally the underlying abelian sheaf morphism of alpha.over (U i). Functoriality of SheafOfModules.toSheaf sends the assumed local module isomorphism to this local abelian sheaf isomorphism.

Apply Mathlib CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isIso_of_coversTop to obtain the global abelian sheaf isomorphism. Reflect it through SheafOfModules.toSheaf to obtain IsIso alpha. The Mathlib cover criterion glues the local inverses, performing the gluing and uniqueness argument of the original plan without a dependency on the project gluing theorem.
